events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Deadly Toll

options.text: Send additional aid to the cities.
Assure the populace that all is well.

events.text: The strange illness stalking [rival] has not disappeared. On the contrary, fear and illness have spread across the countryside in equal measure.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: A Plague Upon Us

options.text: [character] must be Incubated at once!
I cannot give [character] special treatment while all of [rival] suffers.
Only by appeasing the gods shall we be saved.

events.text: The [event] arrives first in the capital and spreads quickly through [rival]. It is not long before your heir, [character], falls into a fevered state, his breath a feeble rattling in the chest.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: A Ship of One’s Own

options.text: Very well. Be careful out there.
Now is not the time for sailing!

events.text: Winds shrill and raucous sing a discordant chorus as waves batter the [rival] coastline. Behind the protection of the city walls, [character] approaches you with a request. Despite the raging [event], [character] wishes to set sail at once in order to aid our naval efforts. Having personally milled several planks and fixed many of the tenons that sturdy a particular [unit], [character] is adamant that he be assigned as captain of the ship.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Test of Engineering

options.text: Structures across [rival] can benefit from the lessons of [city].
[city] shall rise stronger than ever.

events.text: The ground shook in [city], longer and with greater force than had yet been seen. The toll to the city is immense, and yet, the most important buildings still stand. It is near certain that without recent renovations the destruction would have been far worse.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Ablaze

options.text: [city] will recover.

events.text: Despite a cautious eye toward the dry forests, wildfire has come to [city]. Still, the damage could have been worse, had preparations not been made.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: An Uncanny Echo

options.text: I cannot delude myself that they do.
I cannot delude myself that they do not.

events.text: The [event], and the chaos it brings, carries the echoes of your nightmares. Part of you wonders... is it possible your dreams carry the weight of prophecy after all?

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Anger from the Underworld

options.text: [character] is right. We must remove all traces of the shrine at once!
No, I’m pretty sure it’s the volcano.
Convince [character] that the gods are not angry with us.

events.text: The [event] near [city] spews hot ash on the city while laying waste to its surroundings. Overcome with paranoia, [character] is adamant that the [improvement] is the cause of the destruction, acting as a direct channel to the fires of the underworld.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Ashen Descent

options.text: [character] knew there was little to be done but to flee.
His tutor reports that [character] searched for his friend until all hope was lost.
[character] learned much about the [event] firsthand but developed a rasping cough from his slow descent.

events.text: [character] was part way up the high slope of the volcano with his friend and their tutor when a deep rumble began underfoot. The peak above burst with little warning, just as the small party began to flee down the mountain. [character] made it home alive, but his friend was lost in the smoke and hot ash. You question the survivors to learn more details.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Ashfall

options.text: Dump it in the river?
Gather it all into a pile somewhere, I suppose.
Add the ash to the mix for our city’s fortifications.

requirements.label: Cultivator / Steward Of The Land
tip: The leader must have one of: Cultivator; Steward Of The Land (a character trait)

options.text: Use the ash to fertilize our soils.

events.text: [city] lies covered in ash from the [event]. The cleanup process will take time. What shall we do with all the ash?

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: At the Festival

options.text: Convince [character] to take care immediately.
Enforce strict Quarantine measures to limit the spread of the disease.
Punish the [family] for their role in this calamity.
[rival] must remain united while we deal with this tragedy.

events.text: People from all across [rival] gather to celebrate in [city]. The Festival lasts several days and includes a grand feast complemented by songs from visiting performers and dancing by all. The light mood soon grows heavy as participants begin to fall ill, [character] among them. Not long after the celebration disbands and participants return home, reports of further illness reach the capital. The Plague has spread quickly.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Before the Dark Wall

options.text: Order the farmers to work through the storm to save what food they can.
The people should take shelter.

events.text: Strong winds lean heavy behind the dark wall of dust that stretches up to the sky, ready to topple down upon [city]. The timing could not be worse, as farmers race to gather the season’s harvest from the fields. The crops will be lost to the [event] if we do not hurry.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Blindness

options.text: This is a terrible inconvenience.
See that [character] is compensated for his sacrifice.
Gather [rival]’s most skilled healers. [character] must recover from this.

events.text: Leading his forces, [character] is caught in a [event]. Those present describe a mountain in motion, moving slowly at first and then drawn in quickly by the unfeeling wind, covering all in a stinging darkness. For some, the light did not return. Among them was [character], brought back to the capital ragged and breathless.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Brush Fire

options.text: Ready the land for farming.
Import Camel to graze once the seasons bring life back to the burned land.
Leave the area as it is, that the forest might reclaim it.

events.text: The [event] near [city] has spread beyond the forest and scorched a nearby area of Scrub. Some among the city council see this as an opportunity for the land to be put to better use, now that it is cleared.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Buried

options.text: Offer condolences to the [family].
Divine forces are beyond my control.
Pay them off to keep them quiet.
Make known your plan to rebuild the prison with room for many [family].

events.text: The [event] strikes without warning in [city], shaking the city to rubble and dust. The city’s prison lies buried in ruin, [character] among the lost prisoners. The [family] are furious and demand answers.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Carried Away

options.text: Spare no effort in searching for the missing.
[city] must handle its own affairs.

events.text: People, livestock, even entire buildings have been ripped away by the floodwaters in [city].

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Caught in the Flames

options.text: [character] should have been better prepared.
Request that he receive adequate care.
Task our finest healers with [character]’s recovery.

events.text: Word reaches you that [character] was part of a hunting party returning home through the woods near [city] when their path was blocked by the [event]. They turned back in search of an alternate route, but the flames came on quickly from both sides, fanned by heavy winds. The party was separated in the panic, and not all made it home. [character] was among those badly burned. You haven’t been on the best of terms with [character] and must decide what level of care he receives.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Cruel Gods

options.text: You shall have the authority to root out those that the gods cannot abide.
Go back to your crumbling shrines, [character]. I will not be taking your council in future.

events.text: [character] has been summoned in the wake of the [event]. Once, he promised that deference to the gods was the only way to save [rival], and so, deference was given. And yet, any sign of divine protection appears elusive. "If the gods are yet angry," [character] insists, "there are those that yet anger them. Aid me, great king, in rooting out the heretics who bring such doom upon us, and we shall avert greater calamity still."

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Dark Ash

options.text: Send building supplies to help with repairs.
Deliver food to get the [family] through the coming winter.
We have nothing to spare, but invite displaced citizens to resettle in the capital.

events.text: Dark ash chokes the sky near [city], where they say a river of fire came rushing down the lonely mountain and buried or burned much of the city’s nearby infrastructure. The [family] are in a panic about the [event]. In addition to the destruction, much of the city’s crops are expected to fail from lack of sunlight.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Death Sentence

options.text: Order, above all, must be maintained.
Raise a guard to deal with the miscreants.
I haven’t the time for such affairs.

events.text: Surrounded by misery and decay, even the healthy feel they are living under a death sentence. Believing the [event] will keep them from outliving the consequences of their actions, many in [city] no longer fear the law.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Desperation

options.text: Perhaps we can appease the raiders with an offer of Food.
To arms. They will not take what is ours!
It seems we are not the only ones suffering from the [event].

events.text: As you worry about Food shortages brought on by the [event], word reaches you that a raiding party is bearing down on [city].

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Devastation

options.text: Overcrowding is the least of the issues in [city].

events.text: The Slumbering Beast of [city] has awakened, and all the countryside flees from its rain of fire and terror. Many lie dead and injured, and many more seek any roof under which to lay their heads.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Distant Storm

options.text: Send [character] to learn more about this phenomenon.
This does not affect us.
Give a speech to reassure the people of our safety.
Maybe we should be afraid! Call an emergency meeting.

events.text: [character] brings news from distant lands of great black clouds that sweep in low on the horizon and cover all in darkness. It is said that no light can penetrate the heavy, suffocating dust of the [event]. Although these storms appear to pose no immediate threat to the temperate lands of [rival], your people look to you for reassurance.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Distant Waves

options.text: Agree to provide the resources if [character] will give us military aid.
We can provide assistance in exchange for a tribute of Food.
[character] need only ask.
We are in no position to offer help.

events.text: Tales begin to circulate in [rival] of great, merciless waves crashing upon the distant shores before rushing inland as a massive, unstoppable tide. Not long after the stories emerge, an emissary representing the [tribe] arrives at the capital. The fear in the emissary’s eyes as much as words suggest that the stories are true. The [event] appears to have decimated a [tribe] settlement on the nearby coast, and [character] is requesting supplies to help rebuild.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Down River

options.text: Send the needed supplies to rebuild once the flood has subsided.
Perhaps that land should be repurposed.
Now is a good time to build it back stronger.

events.text: Startled citizens watch the river rise and surge near [city]. It is too great a force to divert, and nothing can be done for the [improvement] as the timbers that make up its great wheel are torn off one by one and carried away down the river.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Drought Adept

options.text: Very well. Let’s see what [character] can do.
There are better ways to prepare for a drought.
Our armies would see greater benefit from conventional training.

events.text: In past years of [event], [character] developed both an intimate knowledge of the land and a sharp military mind. He comes to you now with a proposal that he establish a training regimen in [city] to adapt our soldiers to [event] conditions. [character] goes on to speak of methods of water conservation and how best to take advantage of the unique features of drought afflicted land.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Fire Rages

outcomes.label: Calamities The Fire Rages Option 0 Main
Calamities The Fire Rages Option 0 Fallback

options.text: Let them go where they can.

events.text: The parched and dry forests near [city] have overnight turned into a raging inferno. Caught unprepared, scores of people flee the smoke and flames.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Flood Work

options.text: Push forward and finish the job quickly.
Stop work for now and return when it’s safe.
Dispatch more workers to get the job done safely and on time.

events.text: As [event] waters rise in [city], the worksite for the new [improvement] becomes increasingly dangerous. The [unit] fear they may be swept away and are requesting we delay construction until the [event] subsides.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Food Rations

options.text: We may yet face another [event]. It is best to conserve Food stores.
The [event] has passed. Let the people eat.
Let’s join the citizens and celebrate [city]’s return to prosperity!
Arrest the beggars and cut their rations for a month.

events.text: With the [event] behind us, the citizens of [city] are wondering when local Food Rations will end. Some of the city's boldest voices have been rising in a demand for action.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Fortified

options.text: Not all military experience is born in battle.
See that they have some time to recover.

events.text: Dark clouds stretch across the horizon and sweep over the land, extinguishing the day’s light. Thankfully, your [unit] unit was ready for the [event], having fortified their position prior to its arrival.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: From the Sands

options.text: Dig in. Defense is the only option here.
Strike first, before they can surround us.

events.text: From the dark, pressing clouds of the [event], a fierce [tribe] [unit] emerges. These warriors appear especially adept at combat in the stinging winds and lightless skies. Your [unit] brace themselves.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Guard’s Quarry

options.text: Order the guards to chase down and capture the escaped slaves.
Send additional aid to help rescue those trapped.
I’m sure we can find new volunteers.

events.text: Chaos reigns in [city] as the earth quakes. The steep walls of a nearby Quarry collapse down into the depths. Many of those working the Marble below are crushed under the falling stone. As guards work to free those trapped under the rubble, a group of slaves flees amidst the panic.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Misanchored

options.text: Order [character] to take some time off for sailing lessons.
Replace [character] at once with a more competent general.
It might have happened to anyone.

events.text: The [rival] navy flees the [event] winds that rake the sea jagged. Captain [character], it seems, has left his ship anchored, causing the [unit] to take much more damage than was necessary.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: People of [city]

options.text: Very well. Send [religion] to [city].
This is a tragedy, to be sure, but not due to lack of faith.
I saw this coming. Join [character] in [city] at once.

events.text: The sky darkens to black in [city] as an especially severe [event] strikes the city. Violent winds whip at citizens as they flee, while grating sands gut structures to their bones. It is unlike anything our nation has seen before. [character] approaches you in the aftermath of the [event]. He is adamant that the storm was punishment for the absence of the [religion] faith in [city] and demands that direct action be taken.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Recovery Efforts

options.text: Enlist a workforce to help rebuild.
Salvage what we can from the rubble.
All efforts must be focused on restoring [city].
Reach out to our neighbors to see if they require assistance.

events.text: All of [rival] breaks into disarray over the shuddering earth. Many are lost and much is destroyed in the [event], but there is no time to mourn. How will you lead our nation’s recovery?

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: River Surge

options.text: Ensure the safety of the common folk.
See that our nobles and their possessions are safe.
No need. The city’s Walls will protect all.

events.text: Fed by the heavy rains, the river surges and spills up over the banks near [city]. Workers scramble to save what they can from the [event]. What shall be their focus?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Roaring Darkness

options.text: We must brave the storm, to find those trapped without shelter.

events.text: In the heart of the sandstorm, even daylight is weak, and screams are drowned by the roaring wind.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Sandborn

options.text: Honor the [unit] with a fitting name.
Have these desert warriors lead military drills with our other troops.

events.text: Caught in the desert during a [event], your [unit] finds shelter from the worst of the biting sand and moves under the cover of darkness to improve their position. Where most would panic, your [unit] finds calm under dark, smothering clouds, as though born to the sand.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Sheep on the Run

options.text: Corral the beasts where they are to keep them in place.
Sheep? Why are you bothering me with this?
Spread out the herd so as not to overwork the land.

events.text: The river swells and breaks up over its banks, causing a nearby herd of [resource] to flee to dryer grounds near [city]. The animals are stubborn and unwilling to move elsewhere. What shall we do with them?

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Snakes on a Plain

options.text: The [family] are being paranoid. The snakes are just looking for moisture and shade.
Offer sacrifices to in the hopes that this scourge is cleansed from the land.
It is clear that the snakes worship me as their King!

events.text: Snakes! Coiled in dark cellars, slithering out from under shop stalls, they are turning up everywhere in [city]. As the plains grow barren under the constant sun, some say the creatures are migrating in search of shelter. The [family] disagree and see the snakes’ arrival as a dark omen and warn of troubles to come. Are the snakes merely seeking refuge from the [event], or are greater powers at work?

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Stewards of the Land

options.text: Offer to trade Wood in return for Food.
We have nothing to offer, but thank the [tribe] for their help.
Invite a [tribe] Steward Of The Land to live among us so that we might learn their ways.
Detain the representatives and find out the location of their food caches.

events.text: A small delegation of [tribe] arrives at court as part of routine diplomatic relations. During discussions, you learn much about [tribe] ways. As the original inhabitants of the region, the [tribe] possess a deep-rooted knowledge of the land. They appear to be doing quite well despite the ongoing [event]. Word has spread of our Food shortage, and the [tribe] wish to help.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Stormbound

options.text: I will bring the fool back myself.
Find a way to signal for the errant ship’s return.
[character] is on his own.

events.text: As [rival] braces for the [event] moving in off the coast, you receive notice from a breathless messenger that [character], seemingly emboldened by his reckless peers, is sailing out to meet the coming storm.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Taken by the Sea

options.text: We must learn from this tragedy.
Set aside a day to honor those lost.
Though unfortunate, this is a very timely distraction.
We must do better lest we face further punishment.
We must do better lest we face further punishment.
We must do better lest we face further punishment.

events.text: They gathered on the beaches to watch as the tide retreated well beyond the low water mark with an unnatural swiftness. Curiosity gave way to terror when the sea returned in a great [event], slow but unremitting, a wall of churning white teeth eating up all in its path. Among those unable to reach high ground were [character] and several of his troops, taken by the sea.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Taking Shelter

options.text: With people and valuable goods safe, [city] will rebuild.

events.text: Sand and wind descend upon [city], choking the air and tearing at homes. Fortunately, few of the city's inhabitants were taken by surprise.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The Awaited Storm

options.text: [city] will recover.

events.text: The wind and water crashes against [city] and its Harbor. The costs are high, but most people and vessels find shelter from the tempest.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: The Baths of [city]

options.text: Close the baths. They will be of no use when the people have starved.
[city]’s citizens are on edge as it is. I dare not sow further discontent.
I will meet with the farmers. Surely we can work out a compromise.
Close the baths for “maintenance”. Nobles and those with sufficient coin may still attend.

events.text: The sun weighs heavy in the sky over [city]. Despite the heat, a collective of farmers from surrounding lands has gathered in the city. The group decries the use of water for the local Baths while crops fail against the unyielding [event]. The baths are open to all and fill many needs. The court warns that citizens will likely react poorly if this service is taken from them.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: The Colossus Falls

options.text: Accept help from [character].
Heed the warnings of [character].
I think I can fix this.

events.text: The [event] rattles [city] with such violence that Colossus breaks at the knees and topples along the shore, where it now lies in pieces. [character] has offered to help repair the mighty statue, but [character] warns against it, as he believes the [event] to be a punishment from.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: The Cracked Earth

options.text: Secure what food imports we can.
Begin rationing food supplies.
Store all excess food at once.
The gods will watch over [rival].

events.text: For months, no rain has fallen upon the land. Concerns grow as stunted crops wither in the dry, cracked earth. With no clear sign of when the [event] will end, how will you ease the worries of your people?

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: The Dust Settles

options.text: That’s unfortunate.
Recruit more hands to work the land.
Ensure specialized training for the farmers.
See to the matter personally.

events.text: Much of [city] lies covered in a layer of fine dust, swept in from arid regions by the [event]. With fields covered and many seedlings fully buried, farmers near [city] fear their crops might fail. It will take extra effort to bring in a worthwhile harvest this year.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The Earth Moves

options.text: Send supplies, and troops to manage the crisis.

tip: As leader: +10% Unit Trait Modifier / Siege
As leader: +10% Unit Trait Modifier / Ship

options.text: Focus on repairs.

events.text: Did the people of [city] not heed their divine warning? None are prepared for what is, to all appearances, the heavy hand of a wrathful deity. Homes are no more, ancient edifices are ripped asunder, people are crushed by falling stone. And none can say exactly how many are yet wounded or trapped beneath the rubble.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The Hunger of the Sea

outcomes.label: Calamities Hunger Of The Sea Option 0 Main
Calamities Hunger Of The Sea Option 0 Fallback

tip: As leader: +10% Unit Trait Modifier / Siege
As leader: +10% Unit Trait Modifier / Ship

options.text: What's done is done.

events.text: The wave is beyond all reckoning. Ships and homes smash together in tangled chaos. Those that still live stare dumbfounded at the devastation.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The Mountain Wakes

options.text: At least the mountain itself had only scattered inhabitants. Already, [city] prepares to rebuild.

events.text: [city] watches as its quiet countryside turns to smoke, fire, and chaos.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: The Mourning After

options.text: I shall mourn with the people.
Now is no time for rest.

tip: As leader: Stat Bonus: Improvement Repaired → Rebuilder Oath Repair Improvement
As leader: Stat Bonus: Improvement Finished → Rebuilder Oath Build Improvement
As leader: Stat Bonus: Unit Military Killed → Rebuilder Oath Kill Unit

options.text: Pledge an oath to rebuild [rival].
I will deal with this tragedy in my own way.

events.text: Much of the nation’s hope along with its infrastructure lies in ruin following the [event]. When the shaking stops and those who could be found are pulled from the rubble, a period of mourning sets in across [rival].

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The Sea Grows Dark

options.text: We shall replace what we can.
We must recognize, this storm shall not be the last. [city] cannot be rebuilt as it was.

events.text: Wind, water, and fury lash at [city] from the sea. None can so much as stand in the face of the oncoming gale. Caught unprepared, the people watch as their families and livelihoods are torn from their grasp.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: The Undiscovered World

options.text: So shall begin an era of Exploration for [rival]!

outcomes.label: Calamities Tsunami Explore Discover Six Techs
Calamities Tsunami Explore Discover Eight Techs
Calamities Tsunami Explore Religion Eight Shrines

tip: As leader: +5% State Religion Spread Chance

outcomes.label: Calamities Tsunami Explore Religion Four Monastery

tip: As leader: +5% State Religion Spread Chance

outcomes.label: Calamities Tsunami Explore Religion Four Temple

tip: As leader: +5% State Religion Spread Chance

outcomes.label: Calamities Tsunami Explore Religion Three Cathedral

tip: As leader: +5% State Religion Spread Chance

options.text: I’d rather forget about the whole thing.

events.text: The devastation brought on by the [event] leaves us with many questions. What was the origin of this great wave of destruction? Was it a punishment for our actions or some natural phenomenon we don’t yet understand? There is debate in the court as to whether we ought to set out into the unknown to learn more about the world or if it would be best to focus inward instead.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: The Visions

options.text: Well, they will doubt me no more.
I must discover the extent of my powers out in the world.

events.text: The warning came to you in a vision, but you forgot it in another vision… and then remembered it anew in yet another vision! For months and months, you tried to warn them. But now, too late, the [event] is upon us. Would that they had believed your prophecy and convinced you to use your powers to stop it!

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: The Wash

options.text: Call on [city]’s citizens to strike at our disordered enemy.
Though our enemies, I will not exploit [rival]’s ill fate. Order the [family] to help in the rescue and recovery.
Establish a yearly festival to commemorate this fateful moment!

events.text: Some good news from [city], where [rival] lays siege to the city. A foolhardy [rival] [unit], paying no heed to the rising [event] waters, was swept away by the angry rapids while trying to cross the river. The [family] are calling this an omen and suggest we take further advantage of [rival]’s error.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The Wave Breaks

options.text: As the waters recede, we shall build anew.

events.text: The sea claims much, as a wall of water surges far up and down the coast. Still, most of [city] makes it to the safety of higher ground, as they watch the chaos below.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: The World Ends?

options.text: I must accept that it is.
I cannot accept that it is.

events.text: The [event], and the chaos it brings, carries the echoes of your nightmares. Is this truly to be the end of you, of [rival], of all that you know?

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: To Waver

options.text: Berate [character] for his impiety.
Help [character] restore his faith in.
[character] is right. abandoned us!

events.text: As temples fill with the dead and dying, and bodies pile up on the street, many begin to lose hope. The [event] seems to kill indiscriminately, regardless of one’s piety. With his faith in wavering, [character] comes to you for advice.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: To the Sea

options.text: The bounty of the sea should meet our needs.
[rival] will be fine.

events.text: Crop yields appear grim in the face of mounting [event] conditions. It has been suggested that we secure alternate Food sources immediately.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Tsunami Timber

options.text: [rival] badly needs that Wood.
The recovery of [city] must come first.
Help with recovery efforts, but establish a program to salvage the timber in the future.

events.text: The [event] lays waste to much of the coast near [city]. As the waters recede, they leave behind a great many trees felled by the mighty waves and washed inland. A good deal of Wood could be collected from the timber, but help is also urgently needed in finding survivors and repairing the wreckage near [city].

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Tyranny vs. Tyranny

options.text: Well, if they already see me as a tyrant...

events.text: Although the [event] is over, trouble remains in [city]. Many decried the city’s Quarantine policy even during the plague, declaring it an attack on their freedom and labeling you a tyrant. Now that the [event] is over, perhaps it is time to lift the restriction.

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Unnatural Threat

options.text: We must defend against any who aim to take advantage of the [event].
Perhaps we can broaden our understanding of this phenomenon.
Let’s refine our policies that most closely relate to the [event].
I will handle this in my own way.
